## Brand Strategy
- **Vision:** "Make everyone feel valued at work"
- **Mission:** "Be the go-to spending solution for forward-thinking teams everywhere"
- **Brand Idea:** "Power to your people" -- punchy, empowering, stands for more than just work
- **Brand Values:** Transparency, Equality, Happiness, Focus
- **Positioning:** Focuses on emotional benefits (feeling valued) vs competitors who focus on success/efficiency
- **Brand Archetypes:** Liberator (freedom/equality) + Magician (dreaming big, multiple lenses)
- Comprehensive strategy section (pp. 5-11) with vision, mission, values, idea, positioning, archetypes

## Tone of Voice
- Four voice pillars: Direct, Forward-thinking, Genuine, Unorthodox
- Each pillar has detailed "What does X sound like?" with numbered writing tips
- Tone adapts based on: what we're saying, where, who we're speaking to, mood they're in
- Headlines add a full stop for boldness
- Emoji usage: allowed naturally (notifications, email subjects, social) but never to replace words, never more than two in a row
- Humor style: dry, clever, layered -- not big LOLs or puns; irreverent not try-hard
- Writing guidance: short sentences, everyday words, cut jargon, show don't tell, lead with benefits not problems
- UX copy: clear, logical, easy to scan; "what" before "why"
- Inclusive language; humor never alienating; treats all seniority levels equally

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Exceptionally detailed voice/tone section with before/after UX copy examples (pp. 24-29) -- rare in brand guidelines
- Three distinct headline categories (Functional, Playful, Situational) with worked examples and rationale
- Pop culture references encouraged in ephemeral content but cautioned against dating
- "Pleo rhymes with Rio" pronunciation guide on cover page
- British English used throughout (colour, humour)
- Situational headlines using triplet/rhyming word strings as a distinctive creative device
